newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Rashid Hussain, Kwong Yik suspension extended.
newsitem.headline: Rashid Hussain, Kwong Yik suspension extended.

text.p: The suspension of trading in the shares of Malaysia's Rashid Hussain Bhd, Kwong Yik Bank Bhd and Malayan Banking Bhd has been extended, the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) said on Tuesday.
The KLSE said it has extended the suspension on requests made by the three banks pending the conclusion of a deal under which Maybank plans to sell its entire stake in Kwong Yik to Rashid Hussain.

The extension was granted "in view that the negotiations for the proposal has reached its final stage and the outcome of the negotiations and subsequent approval of the relevant authority is still pending", the KLSE said.
In a separate statement, the KLSE said it has also allowed Rashid Hussain's 20-percent owned associate DCB Holdings Bhd's request to extend the suspension of trading in its shares.
It said that DCB's share suspension concerned a restructuring involving Rashid Hussain, DCB and Kwong Yik Bank and, therefore, linked to the Maybank-Rashid Hussain deal.
The KLSE said all the four shares' suspension has been extended by 10 trading days from Nov 19 to Dec 3.
The shares have been suspended since October 21.
Maybank, Malaysia's largest banking group, is negotiating to sell its 75 percent interest in Kwong Yik to stockbroking group Rashid Hussain.
Analysts speculated that Maybank was asking for 9-10 ringgit for each Kwong Yik share. Kwong Yik, whose stock was last traded at 6.95 ringgit, has a paid-up capital of 327.3 million shares.
Analysts have said Maybank was selling its stake in Kwong Yik to Rashid to raise funds, as well as to meet a Malaysian banking requirement which disallows a bank from holding two banking licences.

If the deal goes through, Rashid is widely expected to inject Kwong Yik into DCB Holdings, the parent of DCB Bank Bhd. The merged bank would be Malaysia's third largest as measured by assets, analysts said.
